scenes.text: Every founder knows this moment. It's nine p.m., you're out for dinner, and your phone buzzes. A refund to approve. A vendor waiting. A calendar clash. Small decisions, but your whole team is stuck until you open the laptop.
This is Greenlight, an approval terminal for Even G2. Requests from Telegram, Gmail and Google Calendar arrive on your glasses as one card, already checked against your own company rules.
Set it up once. Connect your accounts, and write your rules in plain English. Flag expenses above five hundred dollars. Never double-book investor calls. Then pair your glasses with a six-digit code.

Rohan, from a client team, asks for a three-twenty-dollar AWS refund in Telegram. Greenlight reads it, checks your rules, and shows one card: what, who, and a one-line recommendation. One tap to approve. You get three seconds to undo. Then it's done, and Rohan sees the approval right in the chat.

Not everything is a green light. A nine-hundred-dollar vendor invoice arrives by email. Greenlight flags it, because it's over your five-hundred limit. Hold to decline, and a polite reply goes back on the same thread.
A new invite clashes with your investor call. Greenlight flags it against your no-double-booking rule. Decline it, and the calendar updates.
Every tap is logged: who asked, what for, the policy verdict, your decision, and when. Open the dashboard, and the whole trail is there.
Greenlight. Read the request. Trust your rules. Decide in one tap.
